topics.title: What is a group: characteristics, and groups versus crowds, teams, audiences and mobs
topics.ncert_sections: Nature and Formation of Groups: What is a Group?

concepts.learning_objective: Define a group and identify its salient characteristics such as interdependence, roles, norms and a sense of belonging.
Distinguish groups from crowds, teams, audiences and mobs.
Explain how groups satisfy needs for security, status and self-esteem.
Explain how groups help in goal achievement, satisfy social needs and provide knowledge and information.

topics.title: Group formation and Tuckman's stages of group development
topics.ncert_sections: Group Formation; Stages of Group Formation

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how proximity, similarity and common motives and goals facilitate group formation.
Describe Tuckman's stages of forming, storming, norming, performing and adjourning and recognise them in real groups.

topics.title: Group structure: roles, norms, status, cohesiveness and groupthink
topics.ncert_sections: Stages of Group Formation (group structure); Box 7.1 Groupthink

concepts.learning_objective: Explain roles, norms and ascribed versus achieved status as elements of group structure.
Explain group cohesiveness and why extreme cohesiveness may not be in a group's interest.
Describe groupthink, the conditions that favour it and ways to prevent it.

topics.title: Types of groups and the minimal group paradigm
topics.ncert_sections: Type of Groups; Box 7.2 The Minimal Group Paradigm Experiments

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish primary groups from secondary groups.
Distinguish formal groups from informal groups.
Explain ingroup and outgroup perceptions and interpret Tajfel's minimal group paradigm.

topics.title: Social facilitation and social loafing
topics.ncert_sections: Influence of Group on Individual Behaviour: Social Loafing

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish social facilitation from social loafing and describe Latane's findings.
Explain why social loafing occurs on collective tasks.
Suggest ways of reducing social loafing in groups.
Define group polarisation and predict its effect on group decisions.
Explain the three reasons why group polarisation occurs.
